raw_text:
Yo, TGIF. And what a week. Jensen Huang’s personal drama is overshadowing everything, Microsoft is proving why you don't put all your eggs in one cloud basket, and the global supply chain is just flexing its vulnerabilities. Let’s get into it.

Money Talk

- **Nvidia CEO exit sends ripples through markets.**
Jensen Huang, the former face of Nvidia, resigned following an affair linked to an alleged Chinese spy, leaving behind risky AI bets and a legal mess. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is already pointing fingers at Commerce Secretary Lutnick for "leakage" of critical chips to China, and financial advisors are telling clients to re-evaluate their Nvidia exposure. The drama is real, folks, and it’s got national security implications. [S2][S3][S8][S10][S19]

- **Treasury yields climb on Fed rate hike fears.**
The 10-year Treasury yield is up to 5.17% as the market is now pretty convinced the Fed will hike rates again in December. Brace yourselves, borrowing money isn't getting any cheaper, and liquidity is tightening up. [S1]

- **Microsoft's multi-day outage warns of cloud over-reliance.**
Millions of users are still reeling from a nearly two-day global outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and 365. Microsoft says it’s "improving," but this kind of widespread disruption is a massive wake-up call about how much of the modern economy relies on single cloud providers. Think of all the lost productivity – the cost is staggering. [S5][S6][S11]

- **Jaguar Land Rover posts heavy losses amid EV competition.**
JLR reported a £451 million quarterly loss after cutting 4,000 jobs. Their CEO is practically begging the EU and Britain to team up to fend off Chinese EV makers. It seems even luxury brands aren't immune to the brutal efficiency of the Asian automotive machine. [S13]

- **Data center demand remains robust, defying slowdown fears.**
Good news for the AI infrastructure crowd: utility CEOs at a recent conference aren't seeing any slowdown in electricity growth expectations for data centers. This suggests the underlying demand driving the AI boom is still chugging along, so maybe that "slowdown concern" is indeed overblown. [S4]

World Lore

- **Nvidia's Huang out, CFO steps in amid AI and legal mess.**
Jensen Huang's scandalous departure has left Nvidia's CFO stepping into the interim CEO role, inheriting a minefield of "risky AI bets and a legal mess." This isn't just a corporate leadership change; it's a major tremor in the geopolitically charged tech race between the US and China. [S21][S22][S30]

- **US envoys shuttle between Putin and Zelenskyy.**
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were in the Kremlin meeting with Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi, and they’re off to Ireland to see Zelenskyy next. High-level back-channel diplomacy is clearly in overdrive, suggesting some serious moves behind the scenes on the Ukraine conflict. [S23]

- **Lame-Duck Trump embarks on Asia tour post-midterms.**
President Trump is heading to the Philippines and China right after his party took a beating in the midterms. Expect fireworks, as this could be an attempt to reassert influence or, more likely, engage in some "coercion" tactics with U.S. allies. Buckle up. [S28][S26]

- **Indonesia's VP resigns amid academic credential scandal.**
Indonesia's Vice President Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, has resigned after courts questioned his overseas education documents and eligibility. Another day, another political leader brought down by questionable paperwork. [S24]

- **Mossad chief in DC as Netanyahu pushes for Iran war.**
Roman Gofman, the director of Israel's Mossad and a close confidant of Benjamin Netanyahu, is in Washington D.C. for talks with the Trump administration about the ongoing war in Iran. The situation in the Middle East is clearly far from settled, and diplomatic pressure is ramping up. [S18]

Tech Tea

- **Microsoft's cloud apocalypse continues.**
Outlook, Teams, and much of Microsoft's cloud services have been down for nearly two days globally, impacting millions. This isn't just an outage; it's a full-blown "global cloud crisis" and a serious warning for everyone relying on a single vendor for critical infrastructure. LibreOffice is probably having a field day with the tweets. [S5][S6][S11][S37][S45][S49][S51]

- **ChatGPT Wallet enables AI agents to shop for you.**
OpenAI is rolling out "ChatGPT Wallet" to U.S. Pro subscribers, letting AI agents handle your online shopping and checkout. On one hand, convenient; on the other, this could open up a whole new world of accidental purchases and data privacy headaches. [S41]

- **Huang's Nvidia legacy: sex scandal and environmental concerns.**
Beyond the affair with an alleged Chinese spy that led to Jensen Huang's resignation, his tenure at Nvidia is also being critiqued for its environmental impact. Nvidia's AI chips are fueling water- and chemical-intensive factories and draining power grids. The "founder fairy tale" clearly has a dark side. Meanwhile, Arm's Rene Haas was apparently approached for the top job. [S36][S42][S46][S52]

- **Multiple data breaches hit Uber, Brazilian insurer, and more.**
It’s been a rough couple of days for cybersecurity. Uber confirmed hackers stole thousands of drivers' license info via an AI cloud company, Brazil's Caixa insurer exposed names and tax IDs of 7.6 million customers, and North Korean hackers used fake video calls to steal a whopping $400 million in crypto. Change your passwords, people, and double-check those video calls. [S38][S39][S40][S43]

- **New Apple TV 4K hits YouTube snags on launch day.**
Early adopters of the brand new Apple TV 4K are getting a black screen and an error message saying "YouTube is not yet available on this device." Not exactly the seamless user experience Apple usually promises. Someone at Cupertino is probably having a bad Friday. [S48]

Creator Szn

- **Mattel jumps onto TikTok Shop with iconic brands.**
Mattel is launching a TikTok Shop store this week, featuring Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price, and Monster High. It’s a smart move to capture Gen Z and millennial spending directly on the platform where cultural trends are born. [S59]

- **AI is making ad tech a battle of brains, not just bids.**
As AI automates more advertising workflows, the competition is shifting from simply managing campaigns to who can leverage AI to make the smartest decisions. It's becoming a "fight for the brain behind the buy," where strategic insights powered by AI will determine who wins the ad game. [S60]

- **CTV pushes for standardization as smart TV screens become prime real estate.**
Advertisers are increasingly looking beyond traditional in-stream video to the smart TV home screen itself, recognizing its growing importance. This shift is driving a call for greater standardization in Connected TV (CTV) to make ad placement more consistent and effective. [S56]

- **Marketers optimistic for a strong 2026 holiday shopping season.**
Despite ongoing economic pressures, marketers are surprisingly bullish, expecting holiday revenues for 2026 to increase anywhere from 1% to over 31% compared to last year. If they’re right, expect a vibrant end to the year for creators and brands. [S57]

Supply Lines

- **DHL Express injects €55M into new Stockholm gateway.**
DHL is dropping some serious cash, €55 million, into a new Stockholm gateway. This isn't just an upgrade; it's a strategic play to boost capacity and speed in the Nordic region, showing confidence in cross-border trade there. [S80]

- **FedEx beefs up tech oversight with new board appointment.**
FedEx has appointed Katherine Boyle to its board specifically to deepen tech oversight. This signals that digital transformation and leveraging technology are becoming even more critical priorities for the logistics giant, not just a nice-to-have. [S83][S85]

- **Walmart dramatically expands drone delivery network with Zipline.**
Walmart is set to more than double its drone delivery sites, partnering further with Zipline to offer rapid air delivery nationwide over the coming years. Drones are moving from niche novelty to a mainstream last-mile solution for the retail behemoth, changing how goods get to your door. [S68]

- **White House set to extend Jones Act waiver.**
Sources indicate President Trump is likely to extend the Jones Act waiver, which allows foreign-flagged vessels to move cargo between U.S. ports. This helps alleviate domestic shipping capacity constraints and keeps things moving, especially for critical goods. [S63]

- **USPS readies 2027 rate hikes and a permanent fuel surcharge.**
Prepare your wallets: the USPS plans to increase prices by an average of 5.9% for services like Ground Advantage and Priority Mail in January, along with implementing a permanent fuel surcharge. Shipping costs aren't just rising; they're getting a long-term adjustment. [S69]

- **Port of Los Angeles battles elevated rail dwell times.**
The Port of LA is once again seeing frustratingly long wait times for idle containers heading to rail transport, with dwell times exceeding nine days. This bottleneck means delays for goods moving inland and adds yet another layer of complexity to supply chain planning. [S66]

Speed Round

- Nvidia's former CEO really fumbled the bag on the way out.
- Microsoft's outage is a stark reminder that even giants stumble, and maybe you should back up your emails.
- Pope Leo's South America tour is apparently as much about geopolitics as it is about prayer.
- Emergency stockpiling now includes cider and candy canes, which is a very British form of apocalypse prep.
- Jaguar Land Rover is bleeding cash and wants the UK and EU to hold hands against Chinese EV makers.
- North Korean hackers are using fake video calls to steal millions, so maybe don't answer that Zoom from 'Bill Gates'.
- Truck drivers are dying too young, highlighting a health crisis the industry desperately needs to address.
